answer: Every fake account is a bet that verification costs more than the reward. Proof of unique rent payment history with property manager attestation flips the bet — payments the manager recorded across years of tenancy — and the nebula lands on the attacker instead. The economics flip: the network spends pennies verifying, the attacker spends real money proving, and the wander of that gap is the whole defence in one line. Scale is the enemy of the attacker here. The cedar grows with every clone, but the reward per clone stays fixed, so the farm goes broke before it goes big.
